name: Petit Paquet
description: Petit Paquet (also known as 'Turkish Packets' or 'Paquets Turcs') is an 18th-century French game of pure chance and high-stakes gambling. It pits a single 'Banker' against a group of players. The game is played with several small piles (packets) of face-down cards. Players bet on specific piles, and the top cards are revealed one by one. It is a precursor to modern casino games like Baccarat and Pharaoh, known for its elegant simplicity and rapid wealth transfer.

content.text: Petit Paquet (also known as 'Turkish Packets' or 'Paquets Turcs') is an 18th-century French game of pure chance and high-stakes gambling. It pits a single 'Banker' against a group of players. The game is played with several small piles (packets) of face-down cards. Players bet on specific piles, and the top cards are revealed one by one. It is a precursor to modern casino games like Baccarat and Pharaoh, known for its elegant simplicity and rapid wealth transfer.
Dates back to the royal courts of France in the 1700s. It was particularly popular during the 'Turkish Fad' (Turquerie) in Europe, hence the alternative name.
One Banker and any number of Punters (Players).
The Banker splits the deck into several small face-down packets (usually 5 to 10 piles) and one 'Banker Pile' for themselves.
